bp_change.poolable_reason: OLMESARTAN IS THE COMPARATOR IN ALL THREE TRIALS AND THE INTERVENTION IN NONE OF THEM. Read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: NCT00846365 and NCT01033071 test AZILSARTAN medoxomil plus chlorthalidone, and NCT01599104 tests LCZ696 (sacubitril/valsartan). In every one, olmesartan sits in the ACTIVE_COMPARATOR arm. THE TOPIC CONTAINS NO TRIAL IN WHICH ITS OWN TITLED DRUG IS THE INTERVENTION. This is what a drug-name search over trial records produces when it matches a name anywhere in the record rather than resolving it to an arm. It is not a topic with a defect; there is no honest version of the page, because no poolable result is possible for the question the title asks. AUTHORITY: Cochrane Handbook 6.5 (2024) section 10.10.3 -- 'Meta-analysis should only be considered when a group of studies is sufficiently homogeneous in terms of participants, interventions and outcomes to provide a meaningful summary' -- and MECIR Box 10.10.a C62, 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar'. The interventions here are azilsartan, azilsartan and LCZ696. NOTHING IS LOST BY RETIRING IT: the two azilsartan trials are the coherent core of the AZILSARTAN topic, and are recorded there.

bp_change.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that the three trials are poor -- all three are registered, randomised and report their primary. NOT that azilsartan or LCZ696 are ineffective; this page never asked about them. NOT that no olmesartan trial exists -- only that none is on this page.
bp_change.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
bp_change.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.
bp_change.estimand_established_does_not_cover_the_: READ THIS BESIDE `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the SAME QUANTITY. It records NOTHING about what that quantity was measured AGAINST -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. On attr-pn-review the flag is TRUE and correct while the pool combines patisiran against its own saline placebo, vutrisiran against PATISIRAN, and eplontersen against the placebo cohort of a DIFFERENT TRIAL. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: Does olmesartan, as the intervention, improve blood pressure against a comparator? THIS TOPIC CANNOT ASK THAT QUESTION: no trial on this page tests olmesartan as the intervention..

It identifies no trial that can be pooled.

The outcome sought is Change in blood pressure.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

The arm TYPE is what distinguishes an intervention from a comparator; the interventions[] list alone cannot, because ClinicalTrials.gov lists comparators there too.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.whether_this_review_was_prospectively_re: NO PROSPERO REGISTRATION OR PROTOCOL RECORD IS HELD ON THIS OBJECT.
